did_you_know.text: Did you know? Isaiah compares Israel to a barren and abandoned woman and calls her to rejoice, because she will have more children than the woman who lives with her husband.
Did you know? Israel’s restoration is pictured as an expanding tent: she is to enlarge the space of her tent, lengthen its cords, and strengthen its stakes.
Did you know? The expansion described in the chapter includes breaking out to the right and left, possessing nations, and resettling cities that had been desolate.
Did you know? In chapter 5, the relationship between the LORD and Israel is described through several titles: Husband, Maker, Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, and God of all the earth.
Did you know? The contrast between “for a brief moment” and “with great compassion” emphasizes that the abandonment is temporary, while the gathering and compassion are described as abundant.

Did you know? The LORD compares his oath not to be angry with Israel again to his oath to Noah never again to bring a flood upon the earth; this is the chapter’s explicit connection to the story of Noah’s flood.
Did you know? Even if the mountains move and the hills collapse, the LORD’s steadfast love and covenant of peace will not depart or be shaken.

Did you know? Israel’s vision of restoration includes not only rebuilding from the outside but also education: “All your children will be taught by the LORD,” and as a result, the children will have abundant peace.
Did you know? The foundation of Israel’s security is described as righteousness; the chapter connects it with turning away from oppression, fear, and terror.

Did you know? At the end of the chapter, it says that every weapon formed against Israel will not succeed, and every tongue that rises against her in judgment will be condemned; this is presented as the heritage of the LORD’s servants and their righteousness from the LORD.
